post.caption: Black hematite leaves a red streak. The powder is red brown though the stone looks black. Its name comes from haima, the Greek word for blood. NASA's rover found tiny hematite spheres on Mars, nicknamed blueberries. Flat clusters of hematite crystals are called iron roses. Babylonian carvers made hematite cylinder seals about an inch tall. Rolled across wet clay, each one left a picture signature. Egyptians strung hematite beads over four thousand years ago. Leonardo and other Renaissance artists drew with red chalk made from hematite. Jeweler's polishing rouge is the same chemical as hematite. Pure hematite is about 70 percent iron by weight.
